content.comment_body: Hello all, I want to connect a thermocouple to a [article_no] using an expansion module [product_name], but I'm not sure if that's possible. On this website: [url] It shows an analog expansion module [article_no], can I use it with a [product_name] [article_no]? Apologies for my English.

The analog expansion module [product_name] is an output module. It can output either 0-10V or 0/4-20mA. There is an analog input module [product_name]. This can read 0-10V voltage signals or 0/4-20mA current signals. However, attaching a thermocouple directly to a 0-10V input won't work because its voltage is too low. For example, a type K thermocouple only generates a voltage change of 10mV for a temperature change of 200 K. To use a thermocouple, you need an external transducer designed for thermocouples that outputs a 0-10V or 0/4-20mA signal. Alternatively, using a PT100 or PT1000 is possible. There is a dedicated analog input module, [product_name], suitable for these sensors.

I believe the original question is whether a 24V powered analog module can be connected to a 230V [product_name]. The user manual (page 33 of the 07/2016 version) states: "You can only connect digital modules to devices with the same voltage class." "You can connect analog and communications modules to devices of any voltage class." Therefore, a 24V analog module can be connected to a 230V base device, but you need to provide a 24V supply for the analog module.

I don't think so. From the initial question, it's clear the user wants to connect a thermocouple to the 230V [product_name] using a [product_name]. However, they're uncertain if that's the right module, as it's actually an output module.

Sorry for not sharing all details earlier. I do have the external transducer (0–10V), and as you mentioned, the analog input expansion module is [product_name]. My current question is whether the [product_name] can read analog inputs in the 0–10V range. This expansion module works perfectly with both [product_name] and [product_name], I've tested it. Thank you for your answer!

Hi [user_name], The [product_name] works for [product_name] with 230VAC operation. Extension modules are attached to the right side of the base module, and expansion modules are always connected further to the right. Analog expansion modules should be at the farthest right position. If using an analog output module, it should also be at the extreme right. Please refer to the attachment.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members clarified how analog expansion modules interact with a [product_name] system and the original poster's intent to connect thermocouples. The conversation highlighted the distinction between input and output modules, the necessity of using external transducers for thermocouple signals, and addressed voltage supply requirements and compatibility when combining modules of different voltage classes.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to connect analog input signals from a thermocouple, via an external transducer, to the [product_name] base unit using the correct expansion module. They are looking for reliable 0–10V analog readings and straightforward compatibility between base and expansion modules for easy installation.
